# Discussion

This study derived functional player roles for nine EuroLeague seasons from open data. Four roles — ball handler, wing/forward, interior big and rim protector — were reproducible under player-level resampling, a five-role solution that separates perimeter wings from stretch forwards was nearly as stable, and finer partitions, including the seven-cluster solution used earlier on the same data, were not. Ball handlers and rim protectors were tied to the guard and centre positions, whereas the other roles combined positions. Role labels appeared to add information about lineup performance beyond regularised player ratings, but this apparent gain disappeared when roles were restricted to information available before the test period, and the data had little power to detect synergies between roles.

The roles correspond to those most often reported in the literature. The systematic review by Coma Ribes et al. lists floor generals, shooters, versatile players and paint protectors among its recurrent roles and attributes much of the variation between studies to methodological heterogeneity [@ribes2026identifying]. The number of roles reported elsewhere ranges from three in the women's EuroLeague [@pendolareinecke2025exploring] to nine with box-score data [@ibanez2025redefining; @kalman2020lineup], and low reproducibility of archetypes has been reported before [@penner2025player]. Our results indicate that, with box-score, shot-location and assist-network information, four or five roles can be recovered reproducibly, whereas finer partitions are not; in our sensitivity analyses, variable sets without assist-network information gave less stable solutions, although these sets also contained fewer variables, so the two explanations cannot be separated. The instability of a seven-cluster solution on the same data shows that internal validity indices alone do not guarantee a reproducible partition, which supports the review's call for a common standard [@ribes2026identifying]. Finer distinctions may require play-type or tracking information.

The claim that modern basketball is "positionless" was only partly supported. Ball handlers and rim protectors remained mostly guards and centres, respectively. The other two roles combined positions: the wing/forward role was made up mainly of forwards but included a quarter of guards, and interior bigs combined centres and forwards. This agrees with the convergence of power forwards and centres documented in the EuroLeague [@konca2026from] and with compositional descriptions of position in the NBA [@south2024basketball]: in these data, positional overlap occurs mainly between guards and forwards on the wing and between forwards and centres inside, whereas the primary ball handler and the rim protector remain distinct positions.

The lineup analysis illustrates how easily role effects can be overstated. With role labels estimated in each season, role counts improved out-of-time predictions beyond RAPM, a result that would usually be read as evidence that roles matter. The leakage checks showed that this gain depended on role labels that were themselves estimated from the test seasons, which carry information about players new to the league for whom RAPM had no estimate; when only information available before the test period was used, or new players were left without a role, no positive gain remained. Earlier links between roles and success were established without such controls: lineup net rating was modelled from soft cluster memberships alone and was not validated out of sample [@kalman2020lineup], semi-final qualification was regressed on team role counts without player efficiency or playing time [@chen2023modeling], and role proportions were derived from players selected on high plus-minus [@penner2025player]. The role-combination tests used in the thesis showed a second mechanism: when very short lineups were included, the selected "significant" combinations were almost all negative, consistent with lineups that concede runs being substituted quickly, and with a minimum duration their number fell to the level expected by chance. Together with evidence that lineup quality can be predicted from individual player quality [@martonosi2023predicting], the results provide no support for the idea that role composition adds to lineup performance beyond the quality of the players involved. They do not rule it out either: the simulations show that synergies of one point per 100 possessions would be detected only about half the time with segment-level data from nine seasons. For the thesis's seven-cluster solution, a small gain persisted among players seen in training, which suggests that clusters built from box-score production carry some information about player quality beyond RAPM; this deserves separate study.

## Limitations

Segment-level net rating is very noisy, and all models explained little variance in absolute terms; consequently, the synergy test had limited power (about one half for one point per 100 possessions), and its null result excludes only large synergies. Only pairwise role interactions were tested, because higher-order combinations cannot be estimated in samples of this size. Several analytic choices were revised during the study in response to review — the bootstrap scheme, the covariance structure, the variable set and the composition penalty — and the lineup result changed with them; we therefore report all role solutions and both leakage checks rather than a single preferred estimate. The permutation test did not re-select the composition penalty within each permutation. The decision rule for the number of roles was set after exploratory analyses with fewer resamples; applied to the final run, it favoured four roles, whereas the earlier run had favoured five, so both solutions are reported. Defensive behaviour was represented only indirectly by steals, blocks, rebounds and fouls; the partition was almost unchanged when height was added, which indicates that the roles are not driven by body size alone. Silhouette values were low, so roles are best interpreted as regions of a continuum; posterior probabilities are provided for analyses that require soft membership. Finally, the findings are specific to the EuroLeague, but because data and code are open, the analysis can be repeated directly in other leagues.

## Conclusions

Four functional roles, or five when perimeter wings and stretch forwards are separated, describe EuroLeague players reproducibly from open data, whereas finer partitions do not. Ball handlers and rim protectors remain largely tied to the guard and centre positions, whereas the other roles combine positions. Once leakage of information from the test seasons was removed, role composition did not improve the prediction of lineup performance beyond regularised player ratings, and the data were not sufficient to detect or exclude small synergies between roles. Coaches and analysts can use these roles to describe and scout players. Claims that particular role combinations improve lineup performance should be tested against individual player quality, with role information restricted to what was known in advance.
